question.text: A portfolio has Rp = 18%, benchmark Rb = 12%, tracking error (σ of active return) = 4%. Information Ratio is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Information Ratio = active return / tracking error = (Rp - Rb) / sigma(Rp - Rb) = (18 - 12) / 4 = 6 / 4 = 1.50. The Trap: 0.67 inverts the ratio (TE / active return); 4.50 mistakenly divides by a wrong denominator. Note: Formula per NISM-XXI-B workbook (p.376-377): IR is active return divided by the standard deviation of portfolio-minus-benchmark returns.
